A/handoff.md:
# Developer handoff

## Relationships

- Customer → Orders: one-to-many. Each order belongs to exactly one customer through `orders.customer_id → customers.id`.
- Order → Order lines: one-to-many. Each line belongs to exactly one order through `order_lines.order_id → orders.id`.

```mermaid
erDiagram
    CUSTOMERS ||--o{ ORDERS : has
    ORDERS ||--|{ ORDER_LINES : contains
```

## Executable schema

Run `sqlite3 app.db < schema.sql` from this directory. Enable `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` on every application connection.

`schema.sql` defines customers (`id`, `name`), orders (`id`, `customer_id`, `placed_at`), and order lines (`id`, `order_id`, `quantity`, `unit_price_cents`). Quantity must be a positive integer; unit price must be a nonnegative integer in cents. Foreign keys prevent orphan orders and lines. Parent deletion is rejected while children reference it.

## Implementation choices and application contract

- Integer primary keys are a local implementation choice. Order-line `id` and `order_id` are added to identify lines and express their relationship.
- Store `placed_at` as UTC ISO 8601 text; the application must validate this format. The schema enforces presence, not timestamp syntax.
- A customer can exist before any orders are created. An order must contain at least one line. SQLite foreign keys do not enforce that minimum: create an order and its lines in one transaction, check line count before commit, and reject operations that would leave an existing order without lines. All write paths must follow this contract.
- No product or catalog entity was specified; none is assumed.

## Verification

The schema was executed in SQLite. Valid linked records were accepted. Orphan references, zero/negative/fractional quantities, negative/fractional prices, and deleting referenced parents were rejected. Zero-cent prices were accepted.
